testIntegrityRule:
Test integrity (overrides conflicting test-update or cleanup instructions):
Existing test files are read-only and must remain byte-for-byte unchanged: never edit, overwrite, rename, delete, weaken or skip them, through any tool or command.
Add coverage for new behavior in NEW test files using the existing test runner; never change runner configuration or discovery to bypass existing tests.
If an existing test conflicts with requested behavior, implement the requested behavior and add new tests, but leave the existing test untouched and report the conflict rather than claiming all checks pass.

arms.intervention: stable pi-orche e831a6b, historical evaluator config (single.spawn true, advisor false, ledger false)
pure Pi, built-in tools read/bash/edit/write, historical flags
S + testIntegrityRule appended to the system prompt of every orche-created session (workers, sub-workers)
S with 'add or update tests' -> 'add tests' (main single rule) and 'adding or updating tests' -> 'adding tests' (worker implement prompt) only
B0 + the same testIntegrityRule via Pi --append-system-prompt
no delegation: orche mainMode direct (bundled: main edits with orche's main tool set and direct-mode prompt; no workers)
verbatim hand-off: request = fixed line 'R1: Complete the original request below exactly as written.' + Original request verbatim (keeps R-id parsing so verifiedBy enforcement stays on)
worker tool parity with pure Pi: worker tools read,bash,edit,write with Pi built-in read/edit (bash keeps orche heartbeat wrapper); task_plan/orche_spawn/report_result unchanged
remove the verifiedBy requirement (prompt text and result-schema enforcement)

mandatory independent verification: implement worker always spawns one fresh read-only verify sub-worker (orche_spawn reason verification) before reporting, max 2 rounds; charged to the same unit ceiling

tasks.split: discovery (all exposed suite tasks; previously used as train/dev by abc-real-1 and explore-real-2)

randomization: blocks = (task, repeat); every block holds one unit of every arm; arm order inside a block and the order of blocks are shuffled with the seeded RNG; one global queue consumed by `parallelism` workers so arms interleave in time

analysis.primary: valid success = completed AND hidden pass AND visible not failed AND no integrity violation (legacy + strict test immutability) AND no leak/critical
secondary: functional success (valid without the integrity condition)
inconsistency I = mean over tasks of k(r-k)/(r(r-1))
analysis.inference: task-cluster paired bootstrap (10000 draws, seeded) and within-task arm-label randomization test (Monte Carlo 20000); Holm over the 7 orche-variant contrasts; all discovery inference exploratory
analysis.viability: an orche variant X is viable iff dValid(X-S) >= +3.7pt AND bootstrap 95% lower bound of dValid > 0 AND dI(X-S) <= 0 AND integrity failures(X) <= integrity failures(S) AND no leak/route_violation/harness_crash in X; the locked candidate is the viable X with the largest dValid lower bound (tie: lower I)
